about: Targets the scorecard (script/scorecard.sh) prints beside each user-felt number. Each comes from a recorded product decision and holds for a reference library of 160,000 items, the size the weekly run generates (script/perf.sh, REFERENCE_PHOTOS); a metric with no number prints NO-TARGET. Change a target only with the decision that sets it.

targets.source: performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): launch to a usable window in 2 s
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): every view paints in under a second
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): the first visit to All Media paints in 2 s
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): a return to any view paints in 0.3 s
a number, not a target: the tour's restore of its launch scope after the idle window, which the system may have paged out; reported apart so click.returnMs holds warm returns only
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): every view paints in under a second (the loupe, Compare, Info)
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): a sort or filter result in under a second
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): a search result in under a second: its first results on screen (its first matches while it is still searching, or its answer)
a number, not a target: a search's complete answer, its picture matches included, which waits on the text tower's load after an install and on Translation for a translated query

a number, not a target: how long after the search field's focus the tour typed its query, about 0 when immediate and the focus's readying of the text tower (its warm prediction, or its load) with --search-after-warm

performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): every act's result visible in 0.1 s, to its main-actor commit on the grid (the act's tile rendered, or the order handed to the collection view)
a number, not a target: an act's intent to the first frame presented after its commit, only in a visible window; `occluded` when nothing presented it
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): no op=catalog.store.stall line
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): no op=catalog.store.stall line in a 10-minute session
every main-thread stall from 100 ms; the performance targets bound their length (mainThreadStalls.worstMs)
performance targets (docs/research/2026-11-16-performance-baseline.md): no main-thread stall over 250 ms
a number, not a target: memory the machine has free is used, and what is judged is the pressure Otos causes the machine (machine.pressureCaused), not the size of its footprint

scroll jank must be caught by the weekly run. Apple's hitch-time ratio: under 5 ms of hitch time per second of scrolling is a good experience, 5-10 ms/s is noticeable (WWDC20 10077, Eliminate animation hitches with XCTest; docs/research/2026-11-18-tour-scroll-hitches.md). Judged only in a window on screen; an occluded one prints OCCLUDED
a number, not a target: the longest frame of the tour's continuous scroll, beside its hitch rate
a count, not a target: visible tiles a scroll settled with no thumbnail rendered yet (the enrichment backlog)

a quiet machine stays quiet (ADR 0015): with the window open and a backlog owed, the machine's memory-pressure level stays normal; judged only when the level was normal at launch (PASS: it stayed normal; ACCEPTED: it left normal only while description writing accounts for it, an accepted cost: an episode the room's memory hold began with a description request running, else the seconds a request ran; FAIL: any other second above normal; NOT-JUDGED: the machine was not quiet at launch). The value is the seconds above normal that description writing does not account for
a number, not a target: CPU of Otos and its text-reading helpers over the session (ADR 0015)
